subject: Meteorology
title: Lenticular Clouds
description: A fast breakdown of Lenticular Clouds for builders.

hook.text: Smooth, lens-shaped clouds hovering near mountains look so alien that they've been mistaken for UFOs.

buildup.text: Lenticular clouds form when stable air flows over a mountain and oscillates in standing waves on the lee side.

discovery.text: The cloud appears where the wave crests and air cools to condensation—then vanishes where the wave dips.

twist.text: The cloud looks stationary, but air continuously flows through it—forming on one side, dissipating on the other.

climax.text: Pilots avoid lenticular clouds—the wave turbulence near them can be severe enough to damage aircraft.

punchline.text: A cloud that holds still while wind races through it.

quiz.question: Why do lenticular clouds appear stationary?
options: Air flows through them continuously, forming and dissipating
They are attached to the mountain
